title: Playing verses and standards as written
summary: He likes to play the verse and play standards like the original arrangement, as with Tin Roof Blues and Sharkey's additions.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Did y'all play many verses to tunes back in the old days?

Well I always did like to, Dick. I always, whenever I knew a voice of a tune, I always liked to play the last two boys, start the voice and then go into the chorus. The bands, they don't do that, they just forget about their voice. They take off from the court, but a lot of these voices were putter than the choruses. I agree. And a lot of times, I hear bands, they just take off from the chorus and that's it. But whenever I knew the voice of a tune, I'd always like to take the last two boys, let the, well let the whole band make it, you know? There's an introduction, then go into the voice and then the chorus. Sounds a lot nicer, sounds like an arrangement.

He had Stanley come out to my house one night, Stanley Maddison. And, uh, I forget what we was playing. Zero. He says, y'all got this thing written? I said, no. He said, man, it sounds like you arranged it. You know, but it, I was playing it just like the standard. It should be played, you know? But, uh, most of these bands said, yeah, they play it. It's a tune even if it is a standard. Man, they just take off any way they want. And they're gonna sound like the standard. But I think a standard should be played like it was written. Cause it, if it's good enough to be a standard, it's good enough to keep it to the, conform it to the way it was written. You know what they?
Take a number like zero. Or, our society with a mushrat rambling. There's, there's standard numbers that should be played like they were written.

I like something like tenor blues. If you're gonna play that, which I'm kind of tired of. Yeah. Uh, if you're gonna play that, you oughta put all those parts in. Play it like the rhythm kings made it.

That's right. If you're gonna play it, start it from the introduction and, and carry it on through. Just like the, give the trombone man the solo that, that, that took. Take it out.
